- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 2–4% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average if sentiment shifts.
- If sentiment is rising (increasing from 0.4 to 1.0) and price is falling, model underreacts; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven reversal.
